Ticket Assessment Hub

Build ticket quizzes with a private rubric per ticket, collect trainee answers, grade them with Claude, review the scores, and export the results.

About this tool and how it was built What it stores, how grading works, and what it never does

What it is

A staging workspace for trainers to run ticket-based assessments for new Care Specialists: build the quiz, preview the trainee form, collect answers, grade each ticket against its own rubric, review the grade, and track performance by cohort.

It is a prototype. Use fictional trainees and tickets until the team approves it.

Where the data lives

Quizzes, rubrics, submissions and evaluations are saved in this page's shared database. Everyone the page is shared with as Contributor or above reads and edits the same records. Viewers and Commenters see nothing, so rubrics and expected answers stay private to trainers.

Raw trainee answers are saved once and never changed by grading or review.

How grading works

  • Each ticket is graded on its own, against only the rubric and reference material the trainer wrote for it.
  • Claude judges whether the resolution is correct, not whether the wording matches, and must give a reason for every deduction.
  • When the rubric doesn't give enough to judge a criterion, Claude flags it for trainer review instead of guessing.
  • The page clamps every score to the criterion's maximum and adds up totals itself, so Claude's arithmetic is never trusted.
  • Grading runs on the account of the trainer who clicks the button, and asks that trainer's permission the first time.

Trainer review

  • The original Claude grade is kept unchanged. The trainer's edited grade is saved beside it with who approved it and when.
  • Reevaluating creates a new version and keeps the old one for the audit trail.
  • Pass or fail shows only when the quiz has a passing threshold.

Google Forms

  1. After you approve a quiz's preview, the page writes a Google Apps Script for that quiz.
  2. You paste it into a new project at script.google.com and run it yourself. It creates the form closed and unpublished, with one section per ticket and the ticket link at the top.
  3. You open and share the form yourself. Then import the responses here from the linked Google Sheet or a CSV.

The page never creates, opens or shares a form on its own, and never sends messages.

How it was built

  • Built with Claude as a single page published as a claude.ai artifact, in the same style as the Training Agenda Library.
  • Uses the page's shared database for records, Claude for grading, your Google Sheets connector (read only) for response imports, and SheetJS for Excel files.
  • The source is in the ticket-assessment-hub/artifact folder of the training GitHub repository.

Terms used on this page

C and CP
The customer and the cleaning professional.
Rubric
The trainer's private scoring guide for one ticket: criteria, points, deductions, critical errors and auto-fail conditions.
Reference material
Policy context, knowledge base notes and sample answers that Claude uses to grade. Trainees never see it.
Staging form
The in-page preview of the trainee form, used to submit fictional test answers.
Trainer final
The grade a trainer approved, which may differ from the original Claude grade.
